pages.title: Meet Brad Hazen
pages.intro: Brad Hazen brings a background in real estate, Clark County review engineering and land surveying to conversations about homes, land and your next move.
sections: A property perspective shaped by local experience

Brad is a Real Estate Broker with Realty Pro, Inc. His background includes more than two decades of Clark County review engineering and land survey work, alongside more than 22 years in real estate. That experience gives property questions an additional technical perspective.
Homes, land and investment property

His public profile lists residential and commercial real estate, new construction, luxury homes, lots, acreage and investment properties. Start by discussing the property you own or want to buy, and the information you need to make a decision.
A local starting point

Brad’s public profile identifies Vancouver, Battle Ground and Salmon Creek among the areas he serves. Explore the community guides, then talk with him about your location, timing and property priorities.
Connect directly
Reach Brad at (360) 921-9484 or b.hazen@hotmail.com to discuss buying, selling or preparing a listing.

pages.title: Plan your home purchase
pages.intro: Begin with what matters to you: the home, the location, and the timing.
sections: Define your priorities
Share the features you need, your preferred communities, and your ideal moving date. Brad can help you organize a focused starting point.
Prepare for the search
Discuss your buying timeline and the questions you want answered before touring properties. If you need financing, coordinate with your chosen lender.
Make your next move
When you find a property of interest, talk with Brad about the offer process, inspections, and the steps toward closing.
faqs: How do I start?
Share your preferred communities, home features, and timing. If you plan to finance the purchase, speak with your lender about your budget and preparation before making an offer.
Can I search live listings here?
This website does not currently include a live MLS search. Contact Brad to discuss homes you are considering and ask about available search options.
What should I bring to our first conversation?
A list of must-have features, areas you want to explore, your moving timeline, and any questions about the buying process.

pages.title: Sell your property with a clear plan
pages.intro: Start with your goals, bring the property details, and discuss a listing approach with Brad Hazen.
sections: Discuss your goals
Tell Brad about your property, when you hope to move, and what a successful sale would look like for you.
Prepare your property
Identify the information, photos, and preparation needed to present your property. Brad’s specific marketing services will be confirmed in your listing discussion.
Plan the next steps
Review a proposed approach to pricing, marketing, and communication before deciding how to move forward.
faqs: What information helps with a selling plan?
Your property address, major updates, approximate condition, and preferred timing give Brad a useful starting point.
Do I need to make improvements first?
Discuss your property and goals with Brad before committing to preparation work. Ask which items should be reviewed as part of your proposed sale plan.
How do I request a home assessment?
Visit the home assessment page and prepare an inquiry with your address and property details. Brad can explain the next steps for a personal market assessment.
How will my property be marketed?

Explore the listing approach to see how a dedicated property page can support your presentation. Confirm the photography, outreach channels, included services, budget, and communication plan with Brad for your property.

pages.title: A listing approach built around your property
pages.intro: Explore how your property can be presented, shared, and discussed with prospective buyers. Start by planning the details with Brad.
faqs: Does a property page include MLS exposure?
A website property page is separate from MLS distribution. Ask Brad which brokerage and MLS services are included in your listing plan.
Are advertising and photography included?
Confirm the proposed services, responsibilities, fees, and any separate advertising budget with Brad before approving the plan.
Can I start if I am only considering a sale?
Yes. Bring your property details and questions to an initial conversation. The seller checklist can help you organize them.

pages.title: What could your home be worth?
pages.intro: Request a conversation about your property. Brad can explain the next steps for a personal market assessment.
sections: What to have ready
Have your property address, major improvements, approximate condition, and selling timeline ready for your conversation.
A personal starting point
Share your address, improvements, and timing using the inquiry below. This is a request for a conversation, not an instant automated valuation.
faqs: Will I get an instant price?
No. This request starts a conversation about your property; it does not generate an automated value.
What details should I include?
Include your address, recent improvements, any important condition details, and when you might sell. Avoid sending financial documents or sensitive personal information.
How is my inquiry sent?
The form prepares a message in your email application. Review the draft and send it to Brad. If it does not open, copy the prepared message into an email.

pages.title: Privacy information
pages.intro: This preview has no visitor accounts, MLS search, or website inquiry storage. Inquiry forms prepare a message in your email application; you choose whether to send it.
sections: Email inquiries

Form details stay in your browser until you choose to open an email draft. Sending the draft shares those details with Brad through your email provider. Avoid including sensitive financial information.
Hosting

Cloudflare hosts this preview and may process request information to operate and secure the website. A final privacy notice will reflect any future inquiry delivery, analytics, or listing integrations.
Private listing workspace

Authorized editors sign in using Cloudflare email verification. Cloudflare stores listing drafts and uploaded photos. Listing change history records the editor’s sign-in email. Drafts and internal permission notes are private. Publishing makes approved listing details and photos public. Archived drafts and their history remain stored so authorized editors can restore them. Contact Brad about listing information or a data request.
